planting.note: Direct sow into loose, sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; beach evening primrose is a Gulf and Atlantic coastal dune native that tolerates salt spray, wind, and pure sand, making it well suited to beachfront and coastal xeriscape plantings.

directions: Direct sow into loose, sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; beach evening primrose is a low, sprawling native of Gulf and Atlantic coastal dunes, its fleshy, gray-green leaves and large, lemon-yellow flowers opening in the evening and lasting into the following morning, fading to orange-red as they age. It is exceptionally tolerant of salt spray, wind, and pure beach sand, spreading by trailing stems to help stabilize loose dune soil the same way it does in its wild coastal habitat. Unlike the pink-flowered showy evening primrose of inland prairies and gardens, this species is a true beach plant, best used in coastal landscaping, dune restoration, or a sandy, salt-exposed xeriscape bed rather than average garden soil. It needs no supplemental fertilizer and minimal water once established, and self-seeds readily in loose, sunny sand.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into loose, sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; sticky groundcherry spreads by underground rhizomes through beach dunes, sandy prairies, and disturbed sandy ground across the southeastern and Gulf Coastal Plain.

directions: Direct sow or plant divisions into loose, sandy, well-drained soil in full sun. Sticky groundcherry is a low, spreading native perennial of coastal dunes, sandy prairies, and disturbed sandy soils across the southeastern and Gulf Coastal Plain, its finely hairy, gently sticky foliage and stems giving the plant its common name. Small, nodding, pale yellow flowers with a darker throat appear from spring through fall, followed by round yellow fruit enclosed in a papery, lantern-like husk typical of the groundcherry group; the ripe fruit is edible once the husk dries and browns, with a mild, slightly tart flavor. It spreads steadily by underground rhizomes in loose, well-drained sandy soil, making it useful for stabilizing a sunny sandy bank or naturalized dune-edge planting, and it tolerates drought, heat, and poor soil with ease once established.
